findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the nanosecond-integer `created_at` is converted to a git-parseable date before `git rev-list --before=` (e.g. divide by 1e9 and format, or feed `<ns>/1000000000` seconds), since `created_at` is not an ISO date string.
evidence: Plan: 'take the newest main commit at or before the report: git rev-list -1 --before="<created_at>" origin/main'
src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json:42-45 — 'created_at': {'type': ['integer','null'], 'description': 'Creation timestamp in nanoseconds (time.time_ns()).'}
Live ticket JSON shows created_at=1787209401799949001 (ns integer), not an ISO date string
findings.finding: Floor-source #2 prescribes `git rev-list -1 --before="<created_at>" origin/main`, but the ticket schema documents `created_at` as a nanosecond integer (time.time_ns()), which `git --before=` cannot consume as a date without conversion.
scenarios: Step 0 runs the git rev-list command with the raw created_at nanosecond value; git fails to parse it as a date or interprets it as a far-future epoch, yielding no floor or the wrong sha — defeating the purpose of the floor
findings.suggested_fix: State the conversion explicitly: `git rev-list -1 --before="@$(( created_at_ns / 1000000000 ))" origin/main` (git's `@<unix-seconds>` date form), noting created_at is nanoseconds per the ticket schema.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Convert the ticket's nanosecond `created_at` to a git-acceptable date before `git rev-list --before=` (e.g. `--before=@$((created_at/1000000000))` or an ISO-8601 rendering), and state this conversion in Step 0 so the floor SHA is computed against the intended report time.
evidence: Live ticket exemplary-hexahedral-needlefish: "created_at": 1787209401799949001 (raw nanosecond epoch integer)
Plan text: `git rev-list -1 --before="<created_at>" origin/main`
git rev-list --before= expects a date/approxidate string (ISO date or e.g. @<unix-seconds>); a bare 1.78e18 integer is not the intended date and is silently mis-parsed
reducer OMIT_KEYS treats created_at as an epoch too (tests/scripts/reducer/*), corroborating the numeric format
findings.finding: Step 0(b) feeds the ticket's raw `created_at` value directly into `git rev-list -1 --before="<created_at>"`, but `created_at` is a nanosecond-epoch integer (verified live: 1787209401799949001), not a date/approxidate string that `git --before=` accepts. Git will not interpret 1.78e18 as the 2026 report date, so the floor computation silently yields the wrong SHA (whole history or none) — defeating the step's entire purpose.
findings.location: Approach → 'The reported-against floor', source 2 (`git rev-list -1 --before="<created_at>" origin/main`); also AC line 'Step 0 names the two REAL floor sources ... via `git rev-list -1 --before=`'
scenarios: A bug ticket quotes no version; Step 0(b) runs rev-list with the raw ns created_at and records a bogus/empty floor SHA
The hypothesis phase then diffs against a wrong range and treats stale or entire history as in scope — reintroducing the stale-tree diagnosis the step exists to prevent
findings.suggested_fix: In the floor source-2 line, replace `--before="<created_at>"` with a conversion step: derive seconds = created_at // 1_000_000_000 and pass `--before=@<seconds>` (git approxidate accepts the `@<unix-seconds>` form), or format created_at as ISO-8601 first; note explicitly that created_at is a nanosecond epoch, not an ISO string.

evidence: Plan text: "take the newest main commit at or before the report: git rev-list -1 --before=\"<created_at>\" origin/main"
Live ticket exemplary-hexahedral-needlefish: "created_at": 1787209401799949001 — nanoseconds since epoch, not an ISO date
git rev-list --before parses dates, not raw nanosecond integers; a 19-digit value is not a valid git date and will not be interpreted as the 2026 timestamp
findings.finding: Floor source #2's command `git rev-list -1 --before="<created_at>" origin/main` will not work: a rebar ticket's created_at is a nanosecond-epoch integer (verified live: 1787209401799949001), but git --before/--since expects a date string (ISO-8601, RFC2822, relative, or @<unix-seconds>). Passing the raw 19-digit nanos yields a wrong or empty floor SHA silently, defeating the anti-stale-tree purpose.
findings.suggested_fix: State the conversion explicitly, e.g. `git rev-list -1 --before="@$(( <created_at_ns> / 1000000000 ))" origin/main` (git accepts @<unix-seconds>), and note created_at is epoch-nanoseconds so the divide is required.

evidence: Plan: 'take the newest main commit at or before the report: git rev-list -1 --before="<created_at>" origin/main'
src/rebar/schemas/ticket_state.schema.json:42-44: `created_at` is `type: integer`, 'Creation timestamp in nanoseconds (time.time_ns()).'
src/rebar/_engine_support/reads.py:540-541: 'created_at is the CREATE-event timestamp (ns)'

git `--before=` parses dates / `@<unix-seconds>`; a bare nanosecond integer (~1.7e18) is read as seconds far in the future, so `rev-list -1 --before` matches the newest commit — the FLOOR is silently wrong.
findings.finding: Floor source #2 pipes the ticket's `created_at` directly into `git rev-list -1 --before="<created_at>"`, but `created_at` is a nanosecond integer (time.time_ns()), not a date git can parse; git would misinterpret it as a far-future Unix-seconds value and return the newest commit, silently producing a wrong floor.
findings.suggested_fix: State the conversion explicitly, e.g.: `git rev-list -1 --before="@$(( created_at_ns / 1000000000 ))" origin/main`, or convert the ns integer to an ISO-8601 UTC string and pass that to `--before=`. Add an AC that the floor computation is verified against a ticket whose created_at is a known ns value.
